values.description: A multi-step process the agent follows: interview, debug, run a TDD loop, review.
Knowledge and rules the agent applies while it works: best practices, design principles, API references.
Operates a CLI, API, app or bundled script to get something done.
A one-shot action you invoke by name, such as turning the conversation into a PRD.
Changes how the agent talks or behaves for the rest of the session.
An entry point that picks and loads other skills. Retired skills that only redirect count as routers.
One-time configuration or scaffolding of a project, account or tool.

facets.name: Effect
facets.question: What can it change on its own?

values.description: Adds no side effects of its own. It shapes how the agent thinks, writes or reviews. Guidelines and routers are always effect:none, even when the task they support edits code.
Its own steps create or change files, git state or local tools.
Its own steps change something outside your machine: post, send, deploy, provision, file issues, drive a website, or upload data to a service.

facets.name: Needs
facets.question: What do you need besides the agent?

values.description: Instructions only. Works in any agent that supports skills.
A specific command-line tool or desktop app must be installed, such as gh, agent-browser, LibreOffice, Obsidian or a vendor CLI.
An account, API key or paid plan with an outside service.
Drives a real Chromium or Chrome browser.
Relies on the agent being able to spawn subagents.
Reads or writes an issue tracker, GitHub Issues by default.
Needs an MCP server connected.
Uses Claude Code features such as hooks or background agents.
Built for claude.ai artifacts.
Built for the OpenClaw agent.
A verified publisher on its registry (skills.sh, ClawHub or Tencent SkillHub), or the company or maintainer behind the product the skill operates.
Everyone else. Unverified vendor claims default to community.

facets.name: Flags
facets.question: Is there something to check before installing?

values.description: A copy of another publisher's skill under a different org. Each copy found had hundreds of thousands of installs while its original had fewer than twenty, so treat its ranking with caution.
The same publisher ships the skill under two sources, which splits its counts.
The SKILL.md now says the skill is retired and points to a replacement.
Legitimate uses exist, but the same capability can evade bot detection or investigate other people. Read the SKILL.md before installing.

facets.name: Stack
facets.question: Which technologies or services is it about?

facets.name: Security audit
facets.question: What did skills.sh's security scanners report?

values.description: All three skills.sh scanners (Gen Agent Trust Hub, Socket, Snyk) passed.
At least one scanner warned and none failed.
At least one scanner failed.
Not scanned on skills.sh: ClawHub, Tencent SkillHub and domain-hosted skills.

facets.name: Language
facets.question: Is the SKILL.md written in a language other than English?

values.description: The SKILL.md is written in Chinese.
